sources.entry: Stash - Open-source menu bar icon hider for macOS 27 that collapses status items behind a single arrow. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/brentc22/stash) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Stash is a free, open-source macOS 27 menu bar hider that collapses status items behind a single arrow by using a private assessment-mode allowlist.
summary.what_it_does: Stash hides macOS menu bar icons behind one arrow so a crowded bar collapses to a single click, and clicking again brings them back. It targets macOS 27, where the system draws the menu bar as one window, which broke earlier hider apps that enumerated and moved per-item windows. Instead, Stash dlopens the private MenuBarClientCore framework, builds an allowlist of apps that may keep their status items, and activates an assessment-mode assertion with it; collapsing and expanding means swapping that assertion. Per-app hide states (Visible, Hide, Always hide) and a "show while this app is in front" option are configurable in a settings window. Optional features include a global hotkey, auto-collapse delay, hover-to-expand (needs Accessibility permission), a presentation mode that hides everything except the arrow, clock and Control Center, and daily update checks against GitHub Releases. The README says the repository also contains design and plan documents, written in Dutch.
use_cases: hide cluttered menu bar icons on macOS 27
collapse menu bar apps behind one click
clean up the menu bar before a presentation or screen share
keep specific menu bar apps always hidden
open-source alternative to paid menu bar managers
notable: Uses macOS assessment-mode allowlist (private API) instead of moving status item windows, which macOS 27 removed
Per-app Visible / Hide / Always hide settings with a show-while-in-front option
Automatic presentation mode during display mirroring, macOS Screen Sharing or Zoom meetings
Fails safe: if the private API is missing, the arrow shows a warning and nothing gets hidden
Test suite is a plain executable target (swift run StashTests) because XCTest needs Xcode
caveats: Relies on a private framework, so any macOS update may break it and it cannot ship on the Mac App Store
Only tested on one Mac with macOS 27.0 (26A428) according to the README
Hiding works per app, not per icon; no reordering and no separate panel for hidden icons
Must be installed in /Applications for its own arrow to appear; Accessibility permission must be re-granted after each make install or in-app update when the menu bar filter is on
